objects.description: 128-bit identifier type used by systemd APIs. It is a union that exposes the same 128-bit value as either 16 bytes or two 64-bit words. The typedef sd_id128_t names the union for convenient value semantics; functions typically pass/return it by value or via pointers. Suitable for machine/boot/invocation IDs and app-specific IDs; can also be stringified or parsed, including UUID formatting. Construction can occur via macros (e.g., SD_ID128_MAKE) or API functions listed below.

objects.definition:
#define SD_EMERG   "<0>"
#define SD_ALERT   "<1>"
#define SD_CRIT    "<2>"
#define SD_ERR     "<3>"
#define SD_WARNING "<4>"
#define SD_NOTICE  "<5>"
#define SD_INFO    "<6>"
#define SD_DEBUG   "<7>"
objects.description: String macro constants representing syslog-style log level prefixes for stderr messages. Not actual types; they are macros expanding to string literals used to prefix log messages.
Macro constant defining the starting file descriptor number (3) for file descriptors passed via socket activation. Not a type; expands to integer literal.

Opaque event loop context type for systemd’s event API. Forward-declared here; actual structure is defined elsewhere. Managed via sd_event_ref/unref and constructed via sd_event_default or sd_event_new. Represents the main event loop that can watch I/O, timers, signals, children, inotify, and internal events.

Opaque handle representing a single registered event source within an sd_event loop (I/O, timer, signal, child, inotify, defer/post/exit, memory pressure). Forward-declared here; actual structure is defined elsewhere. Lifetime is managed via sd_event_source_ref/unref/disable_unref and it is owned by an sd_event.
Generic event source callback prototype used for defer/post/exit and similar sources. Returns int status; userdata is the pointer set on the source.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_event_io_handler_t)(sd_event_source *s, int fd, uint32_t revents, void *userdata);
objects.description: Callback prototype for I/O events. Receives the watched fd and epoll-style revents mask.
Callback prototype for time events. Receives the scheduled trigger time in microseconds.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_event_signal_handler_t)(sd_event_source *s, const struct signalfd_siginfo *si, void *userdata);
objects.description: Callback prototype for signal events. Receives signalfd_siginfo describing the signal.

Callback prototype for child process events (with siginfo_t when available). On systems without the required feature macros, this typedef degrades to a void* placeholder; callers should compile with appropriate feature macros to use the real prototype.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_event_inotify_handler_t)(sd_event_source *s, const struct inotify_event *event, void *userdata);
objects.description: Callback prototype for inotify events. Receives the inotify_event payload.

Alias for the common systemd destroy-callback type used as a per-source destroy callback. The underlying _sd_destroy_t is defined in another header. Used with sd_event_source_set_destroy_callback/get_destroy_callback.

Anonymous enumeration of enablement modes for event sources. Values: SD_EVENT_OFF, SD_EVENT_ON, SD_EVENT_ONESHOT. Used with sd_event_source_set_enabled and related APIs. As an anonymous enum, there is no distinct named type; constants are provided.
Anonymous enumeration of event loop states returned by sd_event_get_state. Constants define internal lifecycle phases of the event loop.
Anonymous enumeration providing canonical priority constants for event sources. Lower numeric values indicate higher priority. Used with sd_event_source_set_priority/get_priority.

Opaque handle to a systemd journal client context used to open, read, iterate, and query journal entries. The struct is forward-declared and managed via the sd_journal_* API; its layout is intentionally hidden.

Opaque handle for a systemd sd-bus connection object. Only a forward declaration here; actual struct definition is elsewhere. Use through API functions. Details and lifecycle are not defined in this header.
Opaque handle representing a D-Bus message in sd-bus. Forward declaration only; full definition is external.
Opaque handle for a registration slot (e.g., matches, filters, objects) in sd-bus. Forward-declared only.
Opaque handle for a credentials object associated with a bus peer. Forward declaration only here.
Opaque handle tracking a set of bus names/owners, invoking callbacks on changes. Forward-declared only.
Concrete struct describing a D-Bus error: fully qualified name, human-readable message, and an internal flag indicating ownership/cleanup behavior. Used to return error information from sd-bus APIs.
Concrete struct mapping a D-Bus error name to a numeric code (typically errno-like). Useful for translating between error namespaces.
Function pointer type for handling incoming D-Bus messages. Returns int status; may set sd_bus_error. Callback typedef defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_bus_property_get_t) (sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *property, sd_bus_message *reply, void *userdata, sd_bus_error *reterr_error);
objects.description: Function pointer type for serving property GET requests on an object. Produces a reply message.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_bus_property_set_t) (sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *property, sd_bus_message *value, void *userdata, sd_bus_error *reterr_error);
objects.description: Function pointer type for handling property SET requests on an object. Consumes a message carrying the new value.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_bus_object_find_t) (sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, void *userdata, void **ret_found, sd_bus_error *reterr_error);
objects.description: Function pointer type for resolving object instances based on path/interface. Returns found instance via ret_found.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_bus_node_enumerator_t) (sd_bus *bus, const char *prefix, void *userdata, char ***ret_nodes, sd_bus_error *reterr_error);
objects.description: Function pointer type for enumerating child node paths under a prefix. Returns an array of strings via ret_nodes.
Function pointer type invoked when tracked bus names change. Minimal signature: returns int status.
Alias typedef for a destroy/deleter callback type imported from _sd-common.h. Concrete signature is not defined in this header; it matches _sd_destroy_t.

Opaque-style struct used to describe a D-Bus interface vtable for systemd's sd-bus. Each array element represents a start marker, end marker, method, signal, or (writable) property entry, controlled by type and flags. Users should construct arrays of sd_bus_vtable using the provided SD_BUS_* macros; direct field initialization is discouraged. Unused union areas must be zero-initialized if not placed in BSS.

Typedef naming the sd_bus_vtable struct type. Use to declare arrays of vtable descriptors passed to sd-bus registration APIs. Construction is performed via SD_BUS_VTABLE_START, SD_BUS_METHOD/PROPERTY/SIGNAL, and SD_BUS_VTABLE_END macros.
Opaque handle to a systemd D-Bus connection. Only forward-declared/used here; the concrete struct/class definition is not present in this header.
Opaque handle representing a registered match/filter/object/vtable slot on a bus. Only forward-declared/used here; the concrete definition is not present in this header.
Opaque handle for a D-Bus message object (method call/return, signal, or error). Only forward-declared/used here; the concrete definition is not present in this header.
Opaque handle encapsulating peer credentials associated with a bus or message. Only forward-declared/used here; the concrete definition is not present in this header.
Opaque handle used to track a set of peer names/senders and changes thereof on a bus connection. Only forward-declared/used here; the concrete definition is not present in this header.
Error structure used to carry D-Bus error name/message. Only referenced here; full definition is not included in this header. Several helper macros operate on this type.
Mapping entry type for translating D-Bus error names to errno-style codes. Only referenced here; the actual struct definition is not present in this header.
Opaque handle to a systemd event loop object, referenced for attaching a bus to an event loop. Not defined in this header.
Opaque JSON value/variant type used when dumping messages to JSON. Not defined in this header.
128-bit identifier type used throughout systemd APIs. Only referenced here; typedef/struct definition is not in this header.

Opaque monitor handle for sd-login event notifications (seats, sessions, UIDs, machines). Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure layout is private to the library. Instances are created via sd_login_monitor_new() and released with sd_login_monitor_unref().

Opaque handle to the systemd hardware database (hwdb). It represents a reference-counted context used to query key/value properties for a given modalias. Actual structure layout is hidden; interact via the provided API. Lifetime is managed with sd_hwdb_ref/sd_hwdb_unref.

Opaque JSON value handle used by systemd’s JSON API. Represents immutable JSON variants (string, integers, real, boolean, array, object, null). Lifetime is reference-counted via sd_json_variant_ref/unref. The actual struct layout is hidden; only a forward declaration is provided here.

objects.definition:
__extension__ typedef enum _SD_ENUM_TYPE_S64(sd_json_variant_type_t) {
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_STRING,
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_INTEGER,
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_UNSIGNED,
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_REAL,
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_NUMBER, /* This a pseudo-type: we can never create variants of this type, but we use it as wildcard check for the above three types */
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_BOOLEAN,
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_ARRAY,
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_OBJECT,
        SD_JSON_VARIANT_NULL,
        _SD_JSON_VARIANT_TYPE_MAX,
        _SD_JSON_VARIANT_TYPE_INVALID = -EINVAL,
        _SD_ENUM_FORCE_S64(JSON_VARIANT_TYPE)
} sd_json_variant_type_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of possible sd_json_variant types. Includes concrete kinds and helper values (_MAX, _INVALID). Backed by a 64-bit enum via systemd macro.

objects.definition:
__extension__ typedef enum _SD_ENUM_TYPE_S64(sd_json_format_flags_t) {
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_OFF              = 1 << 0,  /* disable json output, make json_variant_format() fail with -ENOEXEC */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_NEWLINE          = 1 << 1,  /* suffix with newline */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_PRETTY           = 1 << 2,  /* add internal whitespace to appeal to human readers */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_PRETTY_AUTO      = 1 << 3,  /* same, but only if connected to a tty (and JSON_FORMAT_NEWLINE otherwise) */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_COLOR            = 1 << 4,  /* insert ANSI color sequences */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_COLOR_AUTO       = 1 << 5,  /* insert ANSI color sequences if colors_enabled() says so */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_SOURCE           = 1 << 6,  /* prefix with source filename/line/column */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_SSE              = 1 << 7,  /* prefix/suffix with W3C server-sent events */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_SEQ              = 1 << 8,  /* prefix/suffix with RFC 7464 application/json-seq */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_FLUSH            = 1 << 9,  /* call fflush() after dumping JSON */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_EMPTY_ARRAY      = 1 << 10, /* output "[]" for empty input */
        SD_JSON_FORMAT_CENSOR_SENSITIVE = 1 << 11, /* replace all sensitive elements with the string "<sensitive data>" */
        _SD_ENUM_FORCE_S64(JSON_FORMAT_FLAGS)
} sd_json_format_flags_t;
objects.description: Bitmask flags controlling JSON formatting and output behavior for sd_json_variant_format/dump.
Bitmask flags affecting JSON parsing; currently supports marking parsed variants as sensitive.

objects.definition:
__extension__ typedef enum _SD_ENUM_TYPE_S64(sd_json_dispatch_flags_t) {
        SD_JSON_PERMISSIVE       = 1 << 0, /* Shall parsing errors be considered fatal for this field or object? */
        SD_JSON_MANDATORY        = 1 << 1, /* Should existence of this property be mandatory? */
        SD_JSON_LOG              = 1 << 2, /* Should the dispatcher log about errors? */
        SD_JSON_DEBUG            = 1 << 3, /* When logging about errors use LOG_DEBUG log level at most */
        SD_JSON_WARNING          = 1 << 4, /* When logging about errors use LOG_WARNING log level at most */
        SD_JSON_STRICT           = 1 << 5, /* Use slightly stricter validation than usually (means different things for different dispatchers, for example: don't accept "unsafe" strings in json_dispatch_string() + json_dispatch_strv()) */
        SD_JSON_RELAX            = 1 << 6, /* Use slightly more relaxed validation than usually (similar, for example: relaxed user name checking in json_dispatch_user_group_name()) */
        SD_JSON_ALLOW_EXTENSIONS = 1 << 7, /* Subset of JSON_PERMISSIVE: allow additional fields, but no other permissive handling */
        SD_JSON_NULLABLE         = 1 << 8, /* Allow both specified type and null for this field */
        SD_JSON_REFUSE_NULL      = 1 << 9, /* Never allow null, even if type is otherwise not specified */
        _SD_ENUM_FORCE_S64(JSON_DISPATCH_FLAGS)
} sd_json_dispatch_flags_t;
objects.description: Bitmask flags modifying behavior of the JSON dispatcher and per-field handling (permissiveness, logging level, nullability, etc.).
Function pointer type for builder callbacks used with SD_JSON_BUILD_CALLBACK; expected to construct a variant and store it in ret.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sd_json_dispatch_callback_t)(const char *name, sd_json_variant *variant, sd_json_dispatch_flags_t flags, void *userdata);
objects.description: Function pointer type for dispatch callbacks invoked during sd_json_dispatch; processes a field named name with the given variant and flags.
Descriptor for mapping JSON object fields to C data structures during dispatch. Specifies expected type, callback, destination offset within userdata, and per-field flags.

Bitmask type carrying flags that apply to a Varlink interface definition. Concrete flag bits are injected via _SD_ENUM_FORCE_S64(SD_VARLINK_INTERFACE_FLAGS) macro from systemd’s enum helpers. Details of available flags are not visible in this header.

objects.definition:
__extension__ typedef enum _SD_ENUM_TYPE_S64(sd_varlink_symbol_type_t) {
        SD_VARLINK_ENUM_TYPE,
        SD_VARLINK_STRUCT_TYPE,
        SD_VARLINK_METHOD,
        SD_VARLINK_ERROR,
        _SD_VARLINK_INTERFACE_COMMENT,     /* Not really a symbol, just a comment about the interface */
        _SD_VARLINK_SYMBOL_COMMENT,        /* Not really a symbol, just a comment about a symbol */
        _SD_VARLINK_SYMBOL_TYPE_MAX,
        _SD_VARLINK_SYMBOL_TYPE_INVALID = -EINVAL,
        _SD_ENUM_FORCE_S64(SD_VARLINK_SYMBOL)
} sd_varlink_symbol_type_t;
objects.description: Enumerates the kinds of symbols in a Varlink interface: named types (enum/struct), method, error, plus special pseudo-symbols for comments.
Bitmask flags that qualify a symbol, primarily methods: whether they support or require the Varlink "more" flag.

objects.definition:
__extension__ typedef enum _SD_ENUM_TYPE_S64(sd_varlink_field_type_t) {
        _SD_VARLINK_FIELD_TYPE_END_MARKER = 0, /* zero type means: this is the last entry in the fields[] array of sd_varlink_symbol */
        SD_VARLINK_STRUCT,
        SD_VARLINK_ENUM,
        SD_VARLINK_NAMED_TYPE,
        SD_VARLINK_BOOL,
        SD_VARLINK_INT,
        SD_VARLINK_FLOAT,
        SD_VARLINK_STRING,
        SD_VARLINK_OBJECT,
        SD_VARLINK_ENUM_VALUE,
        _SD_VARLINK_FIELD_COMMENT,        /* Not really a field, just a comment about a field */
        _SD_VARLINK_FIELD_TYPE_MAX,
        _SD_VARLINK_FIELD_TYPE_INVALID = -EINVAL,
        _SD_ENUM_FORCE_S64(SD_VARLINK_FIELD)
} sd_varlink_field_type_t;
objects.description: Enumerates the possible kinds of fields inside symbols: primitive JSON-like types, composite struct/enum, references to named types, special enum value entries, and comment/end markers.
Direction qualifier for fields in method symbols: regular (not an argument list), input, or output.
Bitmask that modifies field cardinality and nullability: array, map, and nullable.
Describes one field within a symbol (method parameters or members of a struct/enum). It carries type, flags, direction, and either an embedded anonymous symbol or reference to a named type.
Represents a Varlink symbol: method, error, or named type (struct/enum). Contains a flexible array of sd_varlink_field describing its members or arguments.
Top-level Varlink interface definition consisting of a name, flags, and an array of pointers to symbols (methods, errors, and named types).
Bitmask flags controlling formatting of IDL output (e.g., colorization).

Opaque Varlink connection object representing a single client/server connection. Lifetime is managed by sd_varlink_ref()/sd_varlink_unref() and close helpers. Actual structure is not defined in this header.
Opaque Varlink server object managing listening endpoints and multiple sd_varlink connections. Lifetime is managed by sd_varlink_server_ref()/sd_varlink_server_unref().

Bitmask flags describing properties of a reply received or sent over Varlink. ERROR indicates an error reply; CONTINUES indicates more replies will follow; LOCAL marks locally generated replies. Backed by a signed 64-bit enum via systemd helpers.
Bitmask flags passed to method handlers: ONEWAY marks methods without reply; MORE allows multiple notifications before final reply.

objects.definition:
__extension__ typedef enum _SD_ENUM_TYPE_S64(sd_varlink_server_flags_t) {
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_ROOT_ONLY               = 1 << 0, /* Only accessible by root */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_MYSELF_ONLY             = 1 << 1, /* Only accessible by our own UID */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_ACCOUNT_UID             = 1 << 2, /* Do per user accounting */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_INHERIT_USERDATA        = 1 << 3, /* Initialize Varlink connection userdata from sd_varlink_server userdata */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_INPUT_SENSITIVE         = 1 << 4, /* Automatically mark all connection input as sensitive */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_ALLOW_FD_PASSING_INPUT  = 1 << 5, /* Allow receiving fds over all connections */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_ALLOW_FD_PASSING_OUTPUT = 1 << 6, /* Allow sending fds over all connections */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_FD_PASSING_INPUT_STRICT = 1 << 7, /* Reject input messages with fds if fd passing is disabled (needs kernel v6.16+) */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_HANDLE_SIGINT           = 1 << 8, /* Exit cleanly on SIGINT */
        SD_VARLINK_SERVER_HANDLE_SIGTERM          = 1 << 9, /* Exit cleanly on SIGTERM */
        _SD_ENUM_FORCE_S64(SD_VARLINK_SERVER)
} sd_varlink_server_flags_t;
objects.description: Bitmask configuration flags for sd_varlink_server controlling access restrictions, accounting, fd passing policy, and signal handling. Backed by signed 64-bit enum.
Bitmask flags influencing sd_varlink_invocation() behavior, permitting listening and accepting when set.

Opaque udev library context handle. Manages configuration, environment, and logging for libudev operations. Lifetime is reference-counted via udev_ref/udev_unref, constructed with udev_new. Details of internal structure are hidden (incomplete type).

Opaque node in a libudev-generated singly-linked list of key/value entries (e.g., properties, tags, sysattrs). Iterated with udev_list_entry_get_next or udev_list_entry_foreach. Values are accessed via get_name/get_value. Incomplete type; lib manages storage.

Opaque handle representing a device from sysfs/kernel. Provides access to device properties, sysattrs, devnode, subsystem/devtype, parent relationships, and tags. Reference-counted via udev_device_ref/udev_device_unref. Created from syspath, devnum, subsystem+sysname, device id, or environment.

Opaque event monitor for kernel uevents and udev events over netlink. Reference-counted via udev_monitor_ref/udev_monitor_unref. Created with udev_monitor_new_from_netlink, enables receiving and filtering events and can yield udev_device objects.

Opaque enumerator to search sysfs for devices matching filters and to return a sorted list of matching entries. Reference-counted via udev_enumerate_ref/udev_enumerate_unref. Constructed with udev_enumerate_new; produces udev_list_entry via udev_enumerate_get_list_entry.

Opaque handle to query the currently running udev event queue. Reference-counted via udev_queue_ref/udev_queue_unref. Constructed with udev_queue_new; supports checking activity/emptiness, waiting via fd, flushing, and listing queued events (deprecated).

Opaque access object for the static hardware properties database (hwdb). Reference-counted via udev_hwdb_ref/udev_hwdb_unref. Constructed with udev_hwdb_new; can query properties list entries for a given modalias.

functions.name: sd_id128_to_string
functions.signature: char* sd_id128_to_string(sd_id128_t id, char s[_SD_ARRAY_STATIC SD_ID128_STRING_MAX]);
functions.description: Converts a 128-bit ID into a 32-character, lowercase hexadecimal, NUL-terminated string without separators. Intended to serialize sd_id128_t values for logging, files, or IPC. Writes the result into the caller-provided buffer and returns it.
requirements: The output buffer s must be non-NULL and have room for at least SD_ID128_STRING_MAX (33) bytes, including the terminating NUL.
The input id may be any sd_id128_t value; no special initialization is required.
The returned pointer aliases s; the caller owns the buffer.

functions.name: sd_id128_to_uuid_string
functions.signature: char* sd_id128_to_uuid_string(sd_id128_t id, char s[_SD_ARRAY_STATIC SD_ID128_UUID_STRING_MAX]);
functions.description: Converts a 128-bit ID into a UUID-style string (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits with dashes), NUL-terminated. Uses big-endian byte order matching common userspace UUID formatting. Writes the result into the caller-provided buffer and returns it.
requirements: The output buffer s must be non-NULL and have room for at least SD_ID128_UUID_STRING_MAX (37) bytes, including the terminating NUL.
The input id may be any sd_id128_t value; no special initialization is required.
The returned pointer aliases s; the caller owns the buffer.

functions.name: sd_id128_from_string
functions.description: Parses a textual 128-bit identifier into an sd_id128_t. Typical usage is to accept either a plain 32-hex-digit string or a UUID-style string with hyphens and convert it to binary form. Returns a status code and, on success, stores the parsed value in ret. Exact accepted formats and case-sensitivity are not specified in this header and are inferred from naming/systemd conventions.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string representing a 128-bit identifier; exact accepted formats are not specified here (likely 32 hex digits and/or UUID with hyphens).
ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for the result.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (systemd APIs typically return 0 on success and a negative errno-style code on failure; this is inferred, not guaranteed by this header).

functions.name: sd_id128_randomize
functions.description: Generates a new random 128-bit identifier and stores it in ret. Useful for creating unique IDs. Returns a status code indicating success or failure. Details of the RNG and error codes are not documented here and are inferred from systemd conventions.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for the generated ID.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (systemd APIs typically return 0 on success and a negative errno-style code on failure; this is inferred).

functions.name: sd_id128_get_machine
functions.description: Retrieves the machine ID as a 128-bit identifier and stores it in ret. Returns a status code. Exact persistence/source (e.g., /etc/machine-id) and error semantics are not specified in this header but are standard in systemd.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (semantics inferred from systemd: 0 on success, negative errno on failure).

functions.name: sd_id128_get_boot
functions.description: Retrieves the current boot ID as a 128-bit identifier and stores it in ret. Returns a status code. Specific source and error codes are not documented here.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (semantics inferred from systemd).

functions.name: sd_id128_get_invocation
functions.description: Retrieves the invocation ID for the current process context and stores it in ret. Returns a status code. Exact scope and provenance are not specified in this header.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (semantics inferred from systemd).

functions.name: sd_id128_get_app_specific
functions.signature: int sd_id128_get_app_specific(sd_id128_t base, sd_id128_t app_id, sd_id128_t *ret);
functions.description: Derives a stable, application-specific 128-bit ID from the given base ID and an application identifier, and stores it in ret. Intended to produce deterministic per-app IDs bound to a base context. Exact derivation algorithm is not specified here.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
base and app_id must be provided; no other constraints are documented.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (semantics inferred from systemd).

functions.name: sd_id128_get_machine_app_specific
functions.description: Derives a machine-specific, application-specific 128-bit ID using the host’s machine ID as the base and the provided application ID, storing the result in ret. Exact derivation is unspecified here.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
app_id must be provided; no other constraints are documented.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (semantics inferred from systemd).

functions.name: sd_id128_get_boot_app_specific
functions.description: Derives a boot-specific, application-specific 128-bit ID using the current boot ID as the base and the provided application ID, storing the result in ret. Exact derivation is unspecified here.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
app_id must be provided; no other constraints are documented.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (semantics inferred from systemd).

functions.name: sd_id128_get_invocation_app_specific
functions.description: Derives an invocation-specific, application-specific 128-bit ID using the current invocation ID as the base and the provided application ID, storing the result in ret. Exact derivation is unspecified here.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
app_id must be provided; no other constraints are documented.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (semantics inferred from systemd).

functions.name: sd_id128_equal
functions.signature: static __inline__ int sd_id128_equal(sd_id128_t a, sd_id128_t b);
functions.description: Compares two sd_id128_t values for equality using a 128-bit comparison. Returns non-zero if equal, zero otherwise. Intended for fast value comparisons in hot paths (inline).
requirements: a and b may be any sd_id128_t values; no special initialization required.
Return value is an int used as a boolean predicate (non-zero equals true).

functions.name: sd_id128_string_equal
functions.description: Compares a textual representation of a 128-bit ID against a binary sd_id128_t. Typically parses s then checks equality with id. Exact accepted string formats and return semantics on parse failure are not documented here.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string representing a 128-bit identifier; exact accepted formats are unspecified here.
Callers must check the return value; specific values for equality/non-equality/error are not defined in this header.

functions.name: sd_id128_is_null
functions.description: Checks whether the given sd_id128_t is all zeros. Returns non-zero if all bytes are zero, zero otherwise.
requirements: a may be any sd_id128_t value.
Return value is an int used as a boolean predicate (non-zero equals true).

functions.name: sd_id128_is_allf
functions.description: Checks whether the given sd_id128_t is all 0xFF bytes. Returns non-zero if all bytes are 0xFF, zero otherwise.
requirements: a may be any sd_id128_t value.
Return value is an int used as a boolean predicate (non-zero equals true).

functions.name: sd_id128_in_setv
functions.signature: static __inline__ int sd_id128_in_setv(sd_id128_t a, va_list ap);
functions.description: Tests whether a occurs in a va_list of sd_id128_t values, terminated by the sentinel SD_ID128_NULL. Returns non-zero if found, zero if the sentinel is reached without a match. Intended as the va_list backend for sd_id128_in_set().
requirements: ap must point to a sequence of sd_id128_t values, terminated by SD_ID128_NULL, or the function will read past the end and exhibit undefined behavior.
The caller must initialize and finalize the va_list according to C rules (e.g., via va_start/va_end in the wrapper).
a may be any sd_id128_t value.

functions.name: sd_id128_in_set_sentinel
functions.description: Variadic helper that tests whether a matches any of the subsequent sd_id128_t arguments, using SD_ID128_NULL as a required terminator. Returns non-zero if found, zero otherwise. Used by the sd_id128_in_set() macro.
requirements: The variadic argument list must contain zero or more sd_id128_t values followed by the SD_ID128_NULL sentinel; omitting the sentinel causes undefined behavior.
All variadic arguments must have the exact type sd_id128_t as passed; mismatched types result in undefined behavior.
a may be any sd_id128_t value.

functions.name: sd_listen_fds
functions.description: Parse file descriptors passed via systemd socket activation and return the number of descriptors made available to the process. If unset_environment is non-zero, the related environment variables ($LISTEN_FDS, $LISTEN_PID, $LISTEN_PIDFDID, $LISTEN_FDNAMES) are removed. Returned fds are numbered from SD_LISTEN_FDS_START (3) upwards. Ensures FD_CLOEXEC is set on the received fds.
requirements: Call only in a context where systemd socket activation may have passed fds (typically at process start).
If unset_environment != 0, callers must not rely on $LISTEN_FDS, $LISTEN_PID, $LISTEN_PIDFDID, or $LISTEN_FDNAMES after the call.
If the caller requires fds without FD_CLOEXEC, it must explicitly unset FD_CLOEXEC after this call for those fds.
On success, valid fds will be in the range [SD_LISTEN_FDS_START, SD_LISTEN_FDS_START + r - 1], where r is the return value.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_listen_fds_with_names
functions.description: Like sd_listen_fds(), but optionally also returns an array of names associated with the passed file descriptors via $LISTEN_FDNAMES. If unset_environment is non-zero, related environment variables are removed. Unknowns: precise ownership/lifetime and allocation details of the returned names array are not documented here.
requirements: Call only in a context where systemd socket activation may have passed fds.
If unset_environment != 0, callers must not rely on $LISTEN_* env vars after the call.

If names is non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to a location where an array pointer can be stored; the function may set it to reference descriptor names corresponding to fds starting at SD_LISTEN_FDS_START.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.
Memory management and termination of the names array are not specified in this header; consult sd-daemon(3) for exact details.

functions.name: sd_is_fifo
functions.description: Check whether fd refers to a FIFO (named pipe), optionally verifying it corresponds to a FIFO at the given filesystem path. Returns 1 if fd matches the criteria, 0 otherwise, negative on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
If path is non-NULL, it should be the expected filesystem path of the FIFO to verify; if NULL, only the FIFO type check is performed.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_is_special
functions.description: Check whether fd refers to a special character device, optionally verifying it is located at the given path. Returns 1 if fd matches the criteria, 0 otherwise, negative on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
If path is non-NULL, it should be the expected filesystem path of the character device; if NULL, only the device type check is performed.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_is_socket
functions.signature: int sd_is_socket(int fd, int family, int type, int listening);
functions.description: Check whether fd refers to a socket matching the specified family and type and optionally its listening state. family==0 disables family check; type==0 disables type check; listening>0 requires a listening socket, listening==0 requires non-listening, listening<0 skips the check. Returns 1 if fd matches, 0 otherwise, negative on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
If family != 0, it must be a valid socket family (e.g., AF_INET, AF_UNIX).
If type != 0, it must be a valid socket type (e.g., SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_DGRAM).
listening must be >0, 0, or <0 to require listening, require non-listening, or skip check respectively.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_is_socket_inet
functions.signature: int sd_is_socket_inet(int fd, int family, int type, int listening, uint16_t port);
functions.description: Check whether fd is an Internet (AF_INET or AF_INET6) socket matching the given family and type, optional listening state, and optional port. family==0 or type==0 skips the respective checks; port==0 skips the port check. Returns 1 if fd matches, 0 otherwise, negative on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
If family != 0, it should be AF_INET or AF_INET6.
If type != 0, it must be a valid socket type (e.g., SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_DGRAM).
If port != 0, it specifies the port number to match (in host byte order unless otherwise documented in sd-daemon(3); not specified here).
listening semantics as in sd_is_socket().
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_is_socket_sockaddr
functions.signature: int sd_is_socket_sockaddr(int fd, int type, const struct sockaddr* addr, unsigned addr_len, int listening);
functions.description: Check whether fd is a socket of the specified type with the same address as addr (of length addr_len). The listening parameter behaves like in sd_is_socket(). Returns 1 if fd matches, 0 otherwise, negative on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
If type != 0, it must be a valid socket type (e.g., SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_DGRAM).
addr must point to a valid socket address structure of length addr_len; addr_len must match the actual size of the structure.
listening semantics as in sd_is_socket(): >0 require listening, 0 require non-listening, <0 skip check.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_is_socket_unix
functions.signature: int sd_is_socket_unix(int fd, int type, int listening, const char *path, size_t length);
functions.description: Check whether fd is an AF_UNIX socket matching the specified type and (optionally) path. For regular pathname sockets, pass length==0 and the filesystem path in path. For abstract namespace sockets, pass path including the leading NUL byte and set length to the socket name length (including the initial NUL). The listening parameter behaves like in sd_is_socket(). Returns 1 if fd matches, 0 otherwise, negative on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
If type != 0, it must be a valid socket type (e.g., SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_DGRAM).
If path is NULL, no path check is performed; otherwise path must reference the appropriate pathname or abstract name as described.
For abstract namespace sockets, path must include the initial NUL byte and length must include that byte.
For filesystem path sockets, set length to 0.
listening semantics as in sd_is_socket(): >0 require listening, 0 require non-listening, <0 skip check.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_is_mq
functions.description: Check whether fd refers to a POSIX message queue, optionally verifying it has the specified name. Returns 1 if fd matches, 0 otherwise, negative on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
If path is non-NULL, it should be the expected message queue name; if NULL, only the mq type check is performed.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_notify
functions.description: Send a status notification to systemd via $NOTIFY_SOCKET. state is a newline-separated list of KEY=VALUE assignments (e.g., READY=1, STATUS=..., MAINPID=...). If unset_environment is non-zero, the notification-related environment variable may be unset by the call. Returns >0 if notified, 0 if notification is not possible (e.g., not running under systemd), negative on error.
requirements: state must be a valid string containing one or more newline-separated KEY=VALUE assignments as expected by systemd.
Callers should handle return values: >0 success, 0 not delivered, <0 error.
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on $NOTIFY_SOCKET after the call.
Only use documented variables (READY, RELOADING, STOPPING, STATUS, NOTIFYACCESS, ERRNO, BUSERROR, WATCHDOG, WATCHDOG_USEC, FDSTORE, FDSTOREREMOVE, FDNAME) or prefix custom variables with X_.
If signaling readiness, use READY=1; non-readiness signaling is discouraged per notes.

functions.name: sd_notifyf
functions.description: Printf-style variant of sd_notify() that formats the notification message according to format and varargs, then sends it. Returns >0 if notified, 0 if not possible, negative on error.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string producing a sequence of newline-separated KEY=VALUE assignments.
Provide matching varargs for the format string.
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on $NOTIFY_SOCKET after the call.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_pid_notify
functions.signature: int sd_pid_notify(pid_t pid, int unset_environment, const char *state);
functions.description: Send a notification message like sd_notify(), but on behalf of another process identified by pid, provided the caller has appropriate permissions. Returns >0 if notified, 0 if not possible, negative on error.
requirements: pid specifies the process to attribute the notification to; it must refer to a process for which the caller has appropriate permissions (exact policy not specified here).
state must be a valid newline-separated KEY=VALUE string.
If unset_environment != 0, the relevant environment variable(s) for the calling context may be unset; do not rely on them after the call.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_pid_notifyf
functions.signature: int sd_pid_notifyf(pid_t pid, int unset_environment, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Printf-style variant of sd_pid_notify(). Formats a notification message and sends it on behalf of the specified pid. Returns >0 if notified, 0 if not possible, negative on error.
requirements: pid must identify a process for which the caller has sufficient permission to send notifications.
format must be a valid printf-style format string producing KEY=VALUE assignments; supply matching varargs.
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on relevant env vars after the call.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_pid_notify_with_fds
functions.signature: int sd_pid_notify_with_fds(pid_t pid, int unset_environment, const char *state, const int *fds, unsigned n_fds);
functions.description: Like sd_pid_notify(), but also sends the array of file descriptors to the service manager for storage (useful for messages including FDSTORE=1). Returns >0 if notified, 0 if not possible, negative on error.
requirements: pid must identify a process for which the caller has sufficient permission to send notifications.
state must be a valid newline-separated KEY=VALUE string; to store fds, include FDSTORE=1 (usage note; not strictly required by this header).
fds must point to an array of at least n_fds valid file descriptors; n_fds is the number of fds to send.
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on relevant env vars after the call.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_pid_notifyf_with_fds
functions.signature: int sd_pid_notifyf_with_fds(pid_t pid, int unset_environment, const int *fds, size_t n_fds, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Combination of sd_pid_notifyf() and sd_pid_notify_with_fds(): formats a notification message and sends it on behalf of pid together with the provided file descriptors. Returns >0 if notified, 0 if not possible, negative on error.
requirements: pid must identify a process for which the caller has sufficient permission to send notifications.
fds must point to an array of at least n_fds valid file descriptors; n_fds is the number of fds to send.
format must be a valid printf-style format string producing KEY=VALUE assignments; supply matching varargs.
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on relevant env vars after the call.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_notify_barrier
functions.description: Synchronize with systemd’s consumption of prior status notifications. Blocks up to timeout microseconds while ensuring previously sent notifications have been consumed (not necessarily processed). Returns >0 if synchronization succeeded, 0 if $NOTIFY_SOCKET was not set, negative on error.
requirements: timeout is specified in microseconds and is passed to ppoll(2).
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on $NOTIFY_SOCKET after the call.
Call this after sending one or more notifications that you want to ensure have been consumed by systemd.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_pid_notify_barrier
functions.signature: int sd_pid_notify_barrier(pid_t pid, int unset_environment, uint64_t timeout);
functions.description: Like sd_notify_barrier(), but attributes/sends the barrier from the specified pid. Returns >0 if synchronization succeeded, 0 if $NOTIFY_SOCKET was not set, negative on error.
requirements: pid must identify a process for which the caller has sufficient permission to send a barrier message.
timeout is specified in microseconds and is passed to ppoll(2).
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on $NOTIFY_SOCKET after the call.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_pidfd_get_inode_id
functions.description: Retrieve an inode identifier associated with the provided pidfd and store it in *ret. Specific semantics (what inode is returned and under which conditions) are not documented in this header; details unknown.
requirements: pidfd should be a valid pid file descriptor referring to a process (e.g., from pidfd_open()); exact requirements not specified here.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory to receive the result.
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_booted
functions.description: Detect whether the system was booted with systemd as the init system. Returns >0 if yes, 0 if not, negative on error. Note: other sd-daemon APIs work regardless and should not be gated on this.
requirements: Check return value semantics: >0 systemd boot, 0 non-systemd boot, <0 error.
Do not use this to gate use of other sd-daemon functions.

functions.name: sd_watchdog_enabled
functions.description: Query whether systemd expects watchdog keep-alive notifications via sd_notify("WATCHDOG=1"). Returns >0 if expected, 0 if not, negative on error. If usec is non-NULL, it is set to the watchdog timeout in microseconds; clients should typically ping every half of this interval.
requirements: If usec is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory to receive the timeout in microseconds.
If unset_environment != 0, do not rely on the relevant environment variable after the call.
Based on the returned timeout, send periodic sd_notify(0, "WATCHDOG=1") pings (recommendation).
Check for negative return values (errno-style) and handle errors.

functions.name: sd_event_default
functions.description: Obtains a default global sd_event loop object and stores it in ret. Intended for code that wants to share a single event loop instance per process or thread. Returns a reference to the default event object.
requirements: ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the sd_event* result.
The returned sd_event* must be released with sd_event_unref() when no longer needed.

functions.name: sd_event_new
functions.description: Creates a new standalone sd_event loop object and stores it in ret. Use when a private event loop is desired.
requirements: ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event*.
The returned sd_event* must be released with sd_event_unref() when no longer needed.

functions.name: sd_event_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the given sd_event and returns the same pointer. Use to keep an additional reference to an event object.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event* obtained from sd_event_new(), sd_event_default(), or another ref.
Do not pass freed or invalid pointers.

functions.name: sd_event_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of the given sd_event and returns NULL when the object is freed. Use to release ownership of an event object.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event* previously obtained from this API.
After this call, the caller must not use e unless another reference is held.

functions.name: sd_event_add_io
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_io(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, int fd, uint32_t events, sd_event_io_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds an I/O event source to watch fd for the specified epoll-style events (e.g., EPOLLIN/EPOLLOUT). When triggered, callback is invoked with the ready events.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor suitable for epoll.
events must be a valid bitmask of epoll events (e.g., EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT).
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_time
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_time(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, clockid_t clock, uint64_t usec, uint64_t accuracy, sd_event_time_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a timer event source that fires at an absolute time usec for the given clock, with desired coalescing accuracy. Invokes callback when due.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
clock must be a valid clockid_t (e.g., CLOCK_MONOTONIC, CLOCK_REALTIME).
usec is an absolute timestamp in microseconds for the specified clock.
accuracy is a non-negative slack in microseconds for coalescing.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_time_relative
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_time_relative(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, clockid_t clock, uint64_t usec, uint64_t accuracy, sd_event_time_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a timer event source that fires after a relative interval usec for the given clock, with desired coalescing accuracy. Invokes callback when due.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
clock must be a valid clockid_t.
usec is a non-negative relative interval in microseconds.
accuracy is a non-negative slack in microseconds.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_signal
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_signal(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, int sig, sd_event_signal_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a signal event source to deliver occurrences of sig to the event loop, invoking callback with signalfd-style info.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
sig must be a valid signal number.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_child
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_child(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, pid_t pid, int options, sd_event_child_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a child-process event source that notifies about state changes (e.g., exit) of the specified pid, invoking callback with siginfo.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
pid must be a valid process ID to monitor.
options is a bitmask or flags controlling behavior (exact values not specified here).
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_child_pidfd
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_child_pidfd(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, int pidfd, int options, sd_event_child_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a child-process event source using an existing pidfd, invoking callback when the child’s state changes.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
pidfd must be a valid pidfd referring to a process.
options is a bitmask or flags controlling behavior (exact values not specified here).
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_inotify
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_inotify(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, const char *path, uint32_t mask, sd_event_inotify_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds an inotify watch on path for the given mask and invokes callback when matching filesystem events occur.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
path must be a non-NULL filesystem path.
mask must be a valid inotify event mask (IN_*-flags).
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_inotify_fd
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_inotify_fd(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, int fd, uint32_t mask, sd_event_inotify_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds an inotify event source using an existing inotify file descriptor fd with mask and invokes callback on events.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
fd must be a valid inotify instance or watch descriptor file descriptor.
mask must be a valid inotify event mask.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_defer
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_defer(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, sd_event_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a deferred callback that runs when the event loop is idle or at a safe point before returning to the caller.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_post
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_post(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, sd_event_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a post-dispatch callback that runs after other sources are dispatched in an iteration.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_exit
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_exit(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, sd_event_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a callback that is invoked when the event loop is exiting.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_add_memory_pressure
functions.signature: int sd_event_add_memory_pressure(sd_event *e, sd_event_source **ret, sd_event_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a source that triggers when system memory pressure is detected and invokes callback. Specific semantics depend on environment.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created sd_event_source*.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_prepare
functions.description: Prepares the event loop for waiting/dispatching by updating internal state. Typically called before sd_event_wait().
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.

functions.name: sd_event_wait
functions.description: Waits for events to become ready or until timeout elapses, without dispatching handlers.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
timeout is a non-negative timeout in microseconds; use a value appropriate for your timing needs.

functions.name: sd_event_dispatch
functions.description: Dispatches all pending events by invoking their callbacks once, without blocking for new events.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.

functions.name: sd_event_run
functions.description: Runs one iteration of the event loop: waits for events up to timeout and dispatches them.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
timeout is a non-negative timeout in microseconds.

functions.name: sd_event_loop
functions.description: Runs the event loop continuously until it is instructed to exit (e.g., via sd_event_exit or exit-on-idle).
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.

functions.name: sd_event_exit
functions.description: Requests termination of the event loop, setting an exit code retrievable later.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
code is an application-defined integer exit status to be recorded.

functions.name: sd_event_now
functions.description: Returns the current time for the specified clock in microseconds, as seen by the event loop, storing it in ret.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
clock must be a valid clockid_t.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the timestamp.

functions.name: sd_event_get_fd
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor used internally by the event loop (e.g., epoll fd).
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.

functions.name: sd_event_get_state
functions.description: Returns the current state of the event loop (one of the SD_EVENT_* state constants).
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.

functions.name: sd_event_get_tid
functions.description: Returns the thread ID associated with the event loop and stores it in ret.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the TID.

functions.name: sd_event_get_exit_code
functions.description: Retrieves the exit code set for the event loop (e.g., via sd_event_exit) and stores it in ret.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the code.

functions.name: sd_event_set_watchdog
functions.description: Enables or disables systemd-style watchdog event generation in the event loop.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
b is treated as a boolean toggle (0 to disable, non-zero to enable).

functions.name: sd_event_get_watchdog
functions.description: Returns whether systemd-style watchdog support is enabled for the event loop.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.

functions.name: sd_event_get_iteration
functions.description: Returns the current iteration count of the event loop and stores it in ret.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the iteration counter.

functions.name: sd_event_set_signal_exit
functions.description: Controls whether certain signals should cause the event loop to exit automatically.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
b is treated as a boolean toggle.

functions.name: sd_event_set_exit_on_idle
functions.description: Configures the event loop to exit automatically when it becomes idle if enabled.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.
b is treated as a boolean toggle.

functions.name: sd_event_get_exit_on_idle
functions.description: Returns whether exit-on-idle is enabled for the event loop.
requirements: e must be a valid sd_event*.

functions.name: sd_event_source_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an event source and returns the same pointer.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* obtained from this API.

functions.name: sd_event_source_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of an event source and returns NULL when the object is freed.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
After unref, the caller must not use s unless another reference is held.

functions.name: sd_event_source_disable_unref
functions.description: Disables the event source (no further callbacks) and unreferences it, returning NULL when freed.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
After this call, the source will be disabled and the caller must not use s unless another reference is held.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_event
functions.description: Returns the parent sd_event loop that owns this source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_userdata
functions.description: Returns the user data pointer associated with the event source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_userdata
functions.description: Associates an arbitrary user data pointer with the event source and returns the previous value.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
userdata may be any pointer value or NULL.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_description
functions.description: Sets a human-readable description for the event source (for diagnostics/logging).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
description may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string; length and lifetime must outlive the call.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_description
functions.description: Retrieves the description string previously set for the source and stores a pointer to it in ret.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the string pointer.
The returned pointer, if any, is owned by the source; do not free it.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_prepare
functions.description: Sets a prepare callback run before dispatching the source, allowing last-moment adjustments.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
callback must be a valid function pointer or NULL if supported (unknown; pass a valid function to be safe).

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_pending
functions.description: Returns whether the event source has a pending event to be dispatched.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_priority
functions.description: Retrieves the dispatch priority of the event source and stores it in ret.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the priority.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_priority
functions.description: Sets the dispatch priority for the event source (lower values mean higher priority).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
priority should be an integer; recommended to use defined ranges (e.g., SD_EVENT_PRIORITY_IMPORTANT..SD_EVENT_PRIORITY_IDLE).

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_enabled

ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the enabled state.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_enabled
functions.description: Enables, disables, or configures one-shot behavior for the event source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
enabled should be one of SD_EVENT_ON, SD_EVENT_OFF, or SD_EVENT_ONESHOT.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_io_fd
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor associated with this I/O event source.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_io_fd
functions.description: Sets or replaces the file descriptor monitored by this I/O event source.

fd must be a valid open file descriptor.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_io_fd_own
