functions.name: sd_event_source_set_io_fd_own
functions.description: Controls whether the event source takes ownership of its I/O file descriptor (closing it on cleanup).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to an I/O source.
own is treated as a boolean toggle.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_io_events
functions.description: Retrieves the epoll event mask being monitored for this I/O source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to an I/O source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the event mask.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_io_events
functions.description: Sets the epoll event mask to watch for this I/O source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to an I/O source.
events must be a valid epoll events bitmask.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_io_revents
functions.description: Retrieves the last observed epoll revents mask for this I/O source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to an I/O source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the revents mask.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_time
functions.description: Retrieves the absolute trigger time (in microseconds) configured for this timer source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a timer source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the timestamp.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_time
functions.description: Sets the absolute trigger time (in microseconds) for this timer source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a timer source.
usec is an absolute time in microseconds for the source’s clock.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_time_relative
functions.description: Sets the relative timeout (in microseconds) for this timer source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a timer source.
usec is a non-negative relative interval in microseconds.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_time_accuracy
functions.description: Retrieves the coalescing accuracy (slack, in microseconds) configured for this timer source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a timer source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the accuracy value.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_time_accuracy
functions.description: Sets the coalescing accuracy (slack, in microseconds) for this timer source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a timer source.
usec is a non-negative accuracy value in microseconds.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_time_clock
functions.description: Retrieves the clock id used by this timer source and stores it in ret.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a timer source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the clock id.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_signal
functions.description: Returns the signal number associated with this signal event source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a signal source.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_child_pid
functions.description: Retrieves the PID monitored by this child event source and stores it in ret.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a child source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the PID.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_child_pidfd
functions.description: Returns the pidfd associated with this child event source, if any.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a child source.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_child_pidfd_own
functions.description: Returns whether the child pidfd is owned (closed) by the event source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a child source.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_child_pidfd_own
functions.description: Controls whether the event source takes ownership of its child pidfd (closing it on cleanup).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a child source.
own is treated as a boolean toggle.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_child_process_own
functions.description: Returns whether the event source owns the lifecycle of the monitored child process (implementation-specific).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a child source.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_child_process_own
functions.description: Controls whether the event source owns the lifecycle of the monitored child process.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a child source.
own is treated as a boolean toggle.

functions.name: sd_event_source_send_child_signal
functions.signature: int sd_event_source_send_child_signal(sd_event_source *s, int sig, const siginfo_t *si, unsigned flags);
functions.description: Sends a signal to the child process associated with this source, optionally with siginfo payload, using the given flags.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a child source.
sig must be a valid signal number.
si may be NULL or a pointer to siginfo_t describing the signal; structure content must match kernel expectations.
flags is a bitmask; supported values are not specified here.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_inotify_mask
functions.description: Retrieves the inotify event mask configured for this inotify source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to an inotify source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the mask.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_inotify_path
functions.description: Retrieves the watched path for this inotify source and stores a pointer to it in ret.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to an inotify source.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the path pointer.
The returned string pointer is owned by the source; do not free it.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_memory_pressure_type
functions.description: Configures the type/category of memory pressure to monitor for this source (exact values unspecified).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a memory pressure source.
ty must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string indicating type; valid values are not specified here.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_memory_pressure_period
functions.description: Sets the thresholds/periods (in microseconds) used to detect memory pressure for this source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source* referring to a memory pressure source.
threshold_usec and window_usec are non-negative microsecond values.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_destroy_callback
functions.description: Sets a callback to be invoked when the event source is destroyed, for resource cleanup.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
callback must be a valid function pointer or NULL to clear (unknown; pass a valid function to set).

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_destroy_callback
functions.description: Retrieves the currently set destroy callback for the source and stores it in ret.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the callback pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_floating
functions.description: Returns whether the event source is floating (not strongly referenced by the event loop).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_floating
functions.description: Marks or unmarks the event source as floating (lifecycle not tied to the event loop reference).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
b is treated as a boolean toggle.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_exit_on_failure
functions.description: Returns whether the event loop will exit if this source’s callback fails.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_exit_on_failure
functions.description: Controls whether the event loop should exit when this source’s callback indicates failure.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
b is treated as a boolean toggle.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_ratelimit
functions.description: Configures rate limiting for this source: at most burst callbacks per interval_usec.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
interval_usec is a non-negative microsecond interval.
burst is a non-zero maximum number of events allowed per interval.

functions.name: sd_event_source_get_ratelimit
functions.description: Retrieves the currently configured rate limit parameters for this source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
ret_interval_usec must be non-NULL to receive the interval.
ret_burst must be non-NULL to receive the burst value.

functions.name: sd_event_source_is_ratelimited
functions.description: Indicates whether the source is currently being rate limited (callbacks suppressed).
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.

functions.name: sd_event_source_set_ratelimit_expire_callback
functions.description: Sets a callback to be invoked when the rate limit suppression period expires for this source.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.
callback must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: sd_event_source_leave_ratelimit
functions.description: Forces the source out of the rate-limited state immediately, allowing callbacks again.
requirements: s must be a valid sd_event_source*.

functions.name: sd_event_trim_memory
functions.description: Requests the library to release unused cached memory back to the system, if possible.

functions.name: sd_journal_print
functions.description: Print a formatted message to the systemd journal with a syslog-style priority. In typical builds this macro records source location (CODE_FILE, CODE_LINE, CODE_FUNC). Use like printf with priority from <syslog.h> (e.g., LOG_INFO).
requirements: priority must be a valid syslog priority (e.g., LOG_EMERG..LOG_DEBUG)
format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers
May expand to sd_journal_print_with_location via macro unless SD_JOURNAL_SUPPRESS_LOCATION is defined
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure; callers should check return value

functions.name: sd_journal_printv
functions.signature: int sd_journal_printv(int priority, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Variant of sd_journal_print that takes a va_list. Typically records source location via macro expansion in default builds.
requirements: priority must be a valid syslog priority
format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string
ap must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to format
May expand to sd_journal_printv_with_location via macro unless SD_JOURNAL_SUPPRESS_LOCATION is defined
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure; callers should check return value

functions.name: sd_journal_send
functions.description: Send one or more journal fields in the form "FIELD=value" via a printf-style interface. Typically records source location via macro expansion. Use _sd_sentinel_ style (must be terminated per implementation).
requirements: format must be a non-NULL printf-style string producing field assignments (e.g., "MESSAGE=%s")
Variadic arguments must match format specifiers
Must be terminated as required by the implementation (sentinel usage implied by _sd_sentinel_ attribute)
May expand to sd_journal_send_with_location via macro unless SD_JOURNAL_SUPPRESS_LOCATION is defined
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure; callers should check return value

functions.name: sd_journal_sendv
functions.signature: int sd_journal_sendv(const struct iovec *iov, int n);
functions.description: Send multiple pre-built journal fields using an iovec array, each element containing a "FIELD=value" buffer.
requirements: iov must point to an array of at least n struct iovec elements
n must be >= 0; when n > 0, each iov[i].iov_base must be non-NULL and iov[i].iov_len must specify the buffer length
Buffers in iovec should be formatted as "FIELD=value" pairs as required by the journal API
May expand to sd_journal_sendv_with_location via macro in default builds
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure; callers should check return value

functions.name: sd_journal_perror
functions.description: Log the current errno as an error message to the journal, with an optional message prefix. Typically records source location via macro expansion.
requirements: message may be NULL or a string to prefix the errno description (based on common perror semantics; exact behavior may vary)
errno should be set appropriately by the caller before calling
May expand to sd_journal_perror_with_location via macro unless SD_JOURNAL_SUPPRESS_LOCATION is defined
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure; callers should check return value

functions.name: sd_journal_print_with_location
functions.signature: int sd_journal_print_with_location(int priority, const char *file, const char *line, const char *func, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Low-level variant of sd_journal_print that explicitly supplies code location metadata (CODE_FILE, CODE_LINE, CODE_FUNC). Intended to be used by macros.
requirements: priority must be a valid syslog priority
file must point to a string like "CODE_FILE=..."
line must point to a string like "CODE_LINE=..."
func must point to the function name string
format must be non-NULL printf-style; variadic args must match
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_printv_with_location
functions.signature: int sd_journal_printv_with_location(int priority, const char *file, const char *line, const char *func, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of sd_journal_print_with_location, providing explicit code location metadata.
requirements: priority must be a valid syslog priority
file must be a "CODE_FILE=..." string
line must be a "CODE_LINE=..." string
func must be the function name string
format must be non-NULL printf-style; ap must be a valid va_list
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_send_with_location
functions.signature: int sd_journal_send_with_location(const char *file, const char *line, const char *func, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Low-level variant of sd_journal_send that explicitly supplies code location metadata; sends one or more "FIELD=value" fields.
requirements: file must be a "CODE_FILE=..." string
line must be a "CODE_LINE=..." string
func must be the function name string
format must be a non-NULL printf-style string producing field assignments
Variadic arguments must match format specifiers
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_sendv_with_location
functions.signature: int sd_journal_sendv_with_location(const char *file, const char *line, const char *func, const struct iovec *iov, int n);
functions.description: Low-level iovec variant of sd_journal_send that also takes code location metadata.
requirements: file must be a "CODE_FILE=..." string
line must be a "CODE_LINE=..." string
func must be the function name string
iov must point to an array of at least n struct iovec elements containing "FIELD=value" buffers
n must be >= 0; for n>0 each iov element must have valid base and length
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_perror_with_location
functions.signature: int sd_journal_perror_with_location(const char *file, const char *line, const char *func, const char *message);
functions.description: Low-level variant of sd_journal_perror that explicitly supplies code location metadata and logs the current errno.
requirements: file must be a "CODE_FILE=..." string
line must be a "CODE_LINE=..." string
func must be the function name string
message may be NULL or a message prefix
errno should be set appropriately before calling
Returns a negative errno-style value on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_stream_fd
functions.signature: int sd_journal_stream_fd(const char *identifier, int priority, int level_prefix);
functions.description: Create or return a writable file descriptor to stream log messages to the journal, tagged with the given identifier and priority. Optionally add a level prefix to each line.
requirements: identifier should be a short non-NULL string used as SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER
priority must be a valid syslog priority constant
level_prefix controls whether the priority prefix is added (non-zero typically enables)
Returns a non-negative file descriptor on success; negative errno-style error on failure
Caller is responsible for writing to and closing the returned fd

functions.name: sd_journal_stream_fd_with_namespace
functions.signature: int sd_journal_stream_fd_with_namespace(const char *name_space, const char *identifier, int priority, int level_prefix);
functions.description: Like sd_journal_stream_fd but targets a specific journal namespace.
requirements: name_space must be a valid namespace name string (non-NULL)
identifier should be a short non-NULL string used as SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER
priority must be a valid syslog priority constant
level_prefix controls whether the priority prefix is added
Returns a non-negative file descriptor on success; negative errno-style error on failure
Caller is responsible for writing to and closing the returned fd

functions.name: sd_journal_open
functions.description: Open the systemd journal for reading according to the specified flags. Returns a handle via ret.
requirements: ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the opened sd_journal*
flags is a bitmask of SD_JOURNAL_* open flags; use 0 or a combination defined in this header
On success, caller must later call sd_journal_close on the returned handle
Returns negative errno-style error on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_open_namespace
functions.signature: int sd_journal_open_namespace(sd_journal **ret, const char *name_space, int flags);
functions.description: Open the journal for reading in the specified namespace.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL to receive the handle
name_space must be a non-NULL namespace name
flags is a bitmask of SD_JOURNAL_* open flags (namespace-related flags apply)
On success, caller must later call sd_journal_close
Returns negative errno-style error on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_open_directory
functions.signature: int sd_journal_open_directory(sd_journal **ret, const char *path, int flags);
functions.description: Open one or more journal files located under the specified directory path for reading.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL to receive the handle
path must be a non-NULL path to a directory containing journal files
flags is a bitmask of SD_JOURNAL_* open flags
On success, caller must later call sd_journal_close
Returns negative errno-style error on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_open_directory_fd
functions.signature: int sd_journal_open_directory_fd(sd_journal **ret, int fd, int flags);
functions.description: Open journal files referenced by an already opened directory file descriptor.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL to receive the handle
fd must be a valid directory file descriptor
If SD_JOURNAL_TAKE_DIRECTORY_FD flag is set, ownership of fd is transferred to this call (it will be closed by the journal object)
flags is a bitmask of SD_JOURNAL_* open flags
On success, caller must later call sd_journal_close
Returns negative errno-style error on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_open_files
functions.signature: int sd_journal_open_files(sd_journal **ret, const char **paths, int flags);
functions.description: Open specific journal files given by a NULL-terminated array of paths for reading.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL to receive the handle
paths must be a non-NULL array of file path strings; termination requirements follow library conventions (commonly NULL-terminated)
flags is a bitmask of SD_JOURNAL_* open flags
On success, caller must later call sd_journal_close
Returns negative errno-style error on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_open_files_fd
functions.signature: int sd_journal_open_files_fd(sd_journal **ret, int fds[], unsigned n_fds, int flags);
functions.description: Open specific journal files identified by file descriptors for reading.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL to receive the handle
fds must point to an array of at least n_fds valid file descriptors
n_fds specifies number of elements in fds
flags is a bitmask of SD_JOURNAL_* open flags
On success, caller must later call sd_journal_close
Returns negative errno-style error on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_open_container
functions.signature: int sd_journal_open_container(sd_journal **ret, const char *machine, int flags);
functions.description: Open the journal of the specified container/machine name. This API is marked deprecated in the header.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL to receive the handle
machine must be a non-NULL machine/container identifier string
flags is a bitmask of SD_JOURNAL_* open flags
On success, caller must later call sd_journal_close
Deprecated: prefer newer container/namespace mechanisms
Returns negative errno-style error on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_close
functions.description: Close a journal handle and free associated resources. Safe to call with NULL per common systemd patterns (unknown if no-op; treat j as valid handle).
requirements: j must be a handle previously returned by an sd_journal_open* function
After this call, j must not be used again

functions.name: sd_journal_previous
functions.description: Move the read position to the previous entry in the journal.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened sd_journal handle
Returns >0 if the position changed, 0 on beginning-of-file, negative errno-style on failure
The current data context changes; any pointers from prior entry enumeration may become invalid

functions.name: sd_journal_next
functions.description: Move the read position to the next entry in the journal.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened sd_journal handle
Returns >0 if advanced, 0 on end-of-file, negative errno-style on failure
The current data context changes; any pointers from prior entry enumeration may become invalid

functions.name: sd_journal_step_one
functions.description: Advance or rewind by a single entry depending on the advanced flag. Combines next/previous functionality.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened sd_journal handle
advanced indicates direction (non-zero to move forward, zero to move backward)
Returns >0 if moved, 0 at boundary, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_previous_skip
functions.description: Move the read position backward by up to skip entries.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened sd_journal handle
skip is the number of entries to move back
Returns the number of entries moved (>=0) or negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_next_skip
functions.description: Move the read position forward by up to skip entries.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened sd_journal handle
skip is the number of entries to move forward
Returns the number of entries moved (>=0) or negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_realtime_usec
functions.description: Retrieve the wallclock (realtime) timestamp of the current journal entry in microseconds since the epoch.
requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the timestamp
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_monotonic_usec
functions.description: Retrieve the monotonic timestamp of the current entry and the boot ID it is relative to.
requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
ret_monotonic must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the usec value
ret_boot_id may be NULL or a pointer to receive the associated boot ID
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_seqnum
functions.description: Get the sequence number and sequence number ID of the current entry.
requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
ret_seqnum must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the sequence number
ret_seqnum_id may be NULL or a pointer to receive the sequence number ID
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_set_data_threshold
functions.description: Set the data field size threshold for inline retrieval; larger fields may be truncated or require explicit fetching depending on implementation.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
sz specifies the threshold in bytes
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_data_threshold
functions.description: Get the current data field inline size threshold.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
sz must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the threshold
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_data
functions.signature: int sd_journal_get_data(sd_journal *j, const char *field, const void **data, size_t *length);
functions.description: Retrieve the value of a specific field from the current entry. The returned buffer typically contains "FIELD=value" and is valid until the next data-related call or position change.
requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
field must be a non-NULL field name (e.g., "MESSAGE")
data must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the buffer pointer
length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the buffer length
Returned pointer lifetime is limited; do not free; becomes invalid after moving the cursor or restarting/enumerating data
Returns negative errno-style on failure; >0 if found, 0 if not found (based on common API pattern)

functions.name: sd_journal_enumerate_data
functions.description: Enumerate data fields of the current entry. Returns successive "FIELD=value" buffers on each call.
requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
Call sd_journal_restart_data(j) before the first enumeration
data must be non-NULL to receive the pointer; length must be non-NULL to receive size
Returned pointer is only valid until the next data operation or cursor movement
Returns >0 while entries remain, 0 when done, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_enumerate_available_data
functions.description: Like sd_journal_enumerate_data but yields only data currently available without extra I/O, useful for partial retrieval.
requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
Call sd_journal_restart_data(j) before the first enumeration
data and length must be non-NULL
Returned pointer validity is limited to the next data operation or cursor movement
Returns >0 while entries remain, 0 when done, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_restart_data
functions.description: Reset the data enumeration state for the current entry so that enumeration restarts from the first field.
requirements: j must be a valid handle; should be positioned on an entry for enumeration to make sense
Invalidates previously returned data pointers from enumeration

functions.name: sd_journal_add_match
functions.signature: int sd_journal_add_match(sd_journal *j, const void *data, size_t size);
functions.description: Add a match term to the current match list used to filter entries. The buffer typically contains a "FIELD=value" expression.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
data must point to a buffer of size bytes describing a match (usually "FIELD=value")
size must be the size in bytes of the buffer
Use sd_journal_flush_matches to clear filters
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_add_disjunction
functions.description: Insert a logical OR into the current match expression chain.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Should be used after adding at least one match to form meaningful expressions
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_add_conjunction
functions.description: Insert a logical AND into the current match expression chain.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Should be used with existing matches to compose expressions
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_flush_matches
functions.description: Clear all match terms previously added to the handle, resetting the filter to match all entries.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
After flushing, subsequent iteration sees unfiltered entries unless new matches are added

functions.name: sd_journal_seek_head
functions.description: Seek to the beginning (oldest) entry in the journal.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Returns negative errno-style on failure; after success, use sd_journal_next to move to entries

functions.name: sd_journal_seek_tail
functions.description: Seek to the end (newest) entry in the journal.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Returns negative errno-style on failure; after success, use sd_journal_previous to move to entries

functions.name: sd_journal_seek_monotonic_usec
functions.signature: int sd_journal_seek_monotonic_usec(sd_journal *j, sd_id128_t boot_id, uint64_t usec);
functions.description: Seek to the entry at or after the specified monotonic timestamp within the given boot ID.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
boot_id specifies the boot the monotonic timestamp belongs to
usec is a monotonic timestamp in microseconds
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_seek_realtime_usec
functions.description: Seek to the entry at or after the specified realtime (wallclock) timestamp in microseconds since the epoch.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
usec is a realtime timestamp in microseconds since the epoch
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_seek_cursor

functions.name: sd_journal_test_cursor

requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
cursor must be a non-NULL cursor string

functions.name: sd_journal_get_cutoff_realtime_usec

from and to must be non-NULL pointers to receive microsecond timestamps

functions.name: sd_journal_get_cutoff_monotonic_usec
functions.signature: int sd_journal_get_cutoff_monotonic_usec(sd_journal *j, const sd_id128_t boot_id, uint64_t *from, uint64_t *to);
functions.description: Get the oldest and newest monotonic timestamps for a given boot ID present in the opened journal sources.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
boot_id identifies the boot instance
from and to must be non-NULL pointers to receive microsecond timestamps
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_usage
functions.description: Report disk usage in bytes of the journal files currently opened by the handle.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
ret_bytes must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the byte count
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_query_unique
functions.description: Prepare unique-value enumeration for the specified field across all matching entries.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
field must be a non-NULL field name string (e.g., "_SYSTEMD_UNIT")
After calling, use sd_journal_enumerate_unique or sd_journal_enumerate_available_unique and reset with sd_journal_restart_unique
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_enumerate_unique
functions.description: Enumerate unique values of the field set by sd_journal_query_unique. Returns buffers typically formatted as "FIELD=value".
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle and sd_journal_query_unique must have been called
Call sd_journal_restart_unique(j) before the first enumeration sequence
data and length must be non-NULL to receive the pointer and size
Returned pointer validity is limited and may be invalidated by subsequent calls
Returns >0 while values remain, 0 when done, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_enumerate_available_unique
functions.description: Enumerate unique values that are immediately available without additional I/O, for the field set by sd_journal_query_unique.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle and sd_journal_query_unique must have been called
Call sd_journal_restart_unique(j) before the first enumeration sequence
data and length must be non-NULL
Returned pointer validity is limited to the next unique operation
Returns >0 while values remain, 0 when done, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_restart_unique
functions.description: Reset the unique-value enumeration state so that the next sd_journal_enumerate_*_unique call starts from the first value again.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Invalidates previously returned unique-enumeration pointers

functions.name: sd_journal_enumerate_fields
functions.description: Enumerate known field names available in the opened journal sources.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Call sd_journal_restart_fields(j) before the first enumeration
field must be non-NULL to receive the field name pointer
Returned pointer validity is limited and may be invalidated by subsequent calls
Returns >0 while fields remain, 0 when done, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_restart_fields
functions.description: Reset the field-name enumeration so that sd_journal_enumerate_fields starts over.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Invalidates previously returned field-name pointers from enumeration

functions.name: sd_journal_get_fd
functions.description: Return a file descriptor that can be polled to detect changes in the journal (new data or invalidation).
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Returns a non-negative fd on success, negative errno-style on failure
Caller must not close this fd separately unless documented; manage lifetime with the journal handle

functions.name: sd_journal_get_events
functions.description: Return an event mask suitable for use with poll/epoll on the fd from sd_journal_get_fd.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Callers should use the returned mask with poll/epoll
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_timeout
functions.description: Return a timeout in microseconds for use with poll/epoll when waiting on the journal fd.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
timeout_usec must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the timeout
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_process
functions.description: Process pending events on the journal handle after a poll indicates activity, updating internal state.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Should be called after poll/epoll indicates events on sd_journal_get_fd
Returns SD_JOURNAL_* wakeup event type (e.g., SD_JOURNAL_NOP/APPEND/INVALIDATE) or negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_wait
functions.description: Block until there is a journal change or the timeout elapses, and return the wakeup event type.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
timeout_usec specifies maximum wait time in microseconds (may accept special values like (uint64_t)-1 for infinite per common patterns)
Returns SD_JOURNAL_* wakeup event type or negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_reliable_fd
functions.description: Return whether the file descriptor returned by sd_journal_get_fd is reliable across journal rotations (or return an alternative reliable fd).
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Returns non-negative fd or boolean-like indicator depending on implementation; negative errno-style on failure
Caller should follow systemd journal documentation for semantics

functions.name: sd_journal_get_catalog
functions.description: Fetch a human-readable message catalog text for the current entry, if available, based on MESSAGE_ID and other fields.
requirements: j must be positioned on a valid entry
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a newly allocated NUL-terminated string
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned string
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_get_catalog_for_message_id
functions.description: Fetch a human-readable message catalog text for the specified MESSAGE_ID.
requirements: id is the 128-bit message ID to query
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a newly allocated string
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned string
Returns negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_has_runtime_files
functions.description: Check whether runtime (volatile) journal files are present for the opened sources.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Returns >0 if present, 0 if not, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_journal_has_persistent_files
functions.description: Check whether persistent journal files are present for the opened sources.
requirements: j must be a valid, opened handle
Returns >0 if present, 0 if not, negative errno-style on failure

functions.name: sd_bus_interface_name_is_valid

functions.name: sd_bus_member_name_is_valid

functions.name: sd_bus_default

functions.name: sd_bus_default_user

functions.name: sd_bus_default_system

functions.name: sd_bus_open

functions.name: sd_bus_open_with_description

description should be a NUL-terminated string or NULL if unsupported (exact acceptance of NULL not documented)

functions.name: sd_bus_open_user
functions.description: Opens a connection to the user (session) bus.

functions.name: sd_bus_open_user_with_description
functions.description: Opens a connection to the user bus and sets a textual description.

description should be a NUL-terminated string or NULL if allowed (not specified)

functions.name: sd_bus_open_user_machine

functions.name: sd_bus_open_system

functions.name: sd_bus_open_system_with_description

description should be a NUL-terminated string or NULL if allowed (not specified)

functions.name: sd_bus_open_system_machine

machine must be a NUL-terminated identifier of the target machine
Caller must manage lifetime (unref/close)

functions.name: sd_bus_new

functions.name: sd_bus_set_address
functions.description: Configures a bus object to connect to the D-Bus at the specified address string.

address must be a NUL-terminated D-Bus address specification

functions.description: Configures a bus object to connect via executing a helper at path with argv.

path must be a NUL-terminated executable path

functions.name: sd_bus_get_address
functions.description: Retrieves the configured/connected bus address string.

ret must be non-NULL

functions.name: sd_bus_set_bus_client

functions.name: sd_bus_is_bus_client

functions.name: sd_bus_is_server

functions.name: sd_bus_set_anonymous
functions.description: Enables or disables anonymous authentication for the connection.

functions.name: sd_bus_is_monitor

functions.name: sd_bus_set_description

functions.name: sd_bus_negotiate_timestamp

b is a boolean-style int flag

functions.name: sd_bus_negotiate_fds

functions.name: sd_bus_get_creds_mask

functions.name: sd_bus_set_allow_interactive_authorization

b is a boolean-style int flag

functions.name: sd_bus_message_skip
functions.description: Skips elements in the message according to the signature types, advancing the cursor.
requirements: m must be valid and readable.
types must be a valid signature string.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_enter_container
functions.description: Enters a container in the message for reading, validating type and contents signature.
requirements: m must be valid and readable.
type must be a valid container type matching the next element.
contents must match the container's element signature.
Must be balanced with sd_bus_message_exit_container.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_exit_container
functions.description: Exits the current container previously entered for reading.
requirements: m must be valid and currently inside a container.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_peek_type
functions.description: Peeks at the next element's type code and container signature (if applicable) without advancing the cursor.
requirements: m must be valid.
ret_type may be NULL or pointer to receive type code.
ret_contents may be NULL or pointer to receive contents signature string; do not free.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_verify_type
functions.signature: int sd_bus_message_verify_type(sd_bus_message *m, char type, const char *contents);
functions.description: Verifies that the next element matches the given type and contents signature.
requirements: m must be valid.
type must be a valid type code.
contents may be NULL or a signature as appropriate for container types.
Returns >0 on match, 0 on mismatch, or negative on error.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_at_end
functions.description: Checks if the current container (or entire message if complete non-zero) has been fully read.
requirements: m must be valid.
complete is a flag selecting whole-message vs container scope.
Returns >0 if at end, 0 otherwise, or negative on error.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_rewind
functions.description: Rewinds the read cursor to the beginning of the current container or entire message if complete is non-zero.
requirements: m must be valid.
complete is a flag.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_sensitive
functions.description: Marks the message as containing sensitive data to adjust logging/handling.
requirements: m must be valid.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_dump
functions.description: Dumps a human-readable representation of the message to stream f with flags controlling formatting.
requirements: m must be valid.
f must be a valid FILE* for output.
flags is a bitmask; exact values not specified here.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_dump_json
functions.description: Produces a JSON representation of the message body/metadata according to flags, returning an sd_json_variant tree in ret.
requirements: m must be valid.
ret may be NULL or pointer to receive allocated JSON variant; caller must manage per sd-json API (likely unref/free).
flags controls output; specifics unknown.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_get_unique_name
functions.description: Returns the unique name assigned by the bus to this connection (e.g. ":1.42").
requirements: bus must be connected.
unique must be non-NULL; returned pointer is owned by the bus; do not free.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_request_name
functions.signature: int sd_bus_request_name(sd_bus *bus, const char *name, uint64_t flags);
functions.description: Requests ownership of the given well-known bus name with flags.
requirements: bus must be connected.
name must be a valid service name.
flags control queueing/replace behavior; exact bits not specified here.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_request_name_async
functions.signature: int sd_bus_request_name_async(sd_bus *bus, sd_bus_slot **ret_slot, const char *name, uint64_t flags, sd_bus_message_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Asynchronously requests a well-known name; completion is indicated via callback. Returns a slot to manage the request.
requirements: bus must be connected.
name must be a valid service name.
flags control behavior.
callback may be NULL or provided; userdata passed through.
ret_slot may be NULL or receive slot; unref when done.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_release_name
functions.description: Releases ownership of a well-known bus name.
requirements: bus must be connected.
name must be a valid service name currently owned (or queued).
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_release_name_async
functions.signature: int sd_bus_release_name_async(sd_bus *bus, sd_bus_slot **ret_slot, const char *name, sd_bus_message_handler_t callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Asynchronously releases a well-known name; invokes callback on completion. Returns a slot.
requirements: bus must be connected.
name must be a valid service name.
callback may be NULL or provided; userdata passed through.
ret_slot may be NULL or receive slot; unref when done.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_list_names
functions.signature: int sd_bus_list_names(sd_bus *bus, char ***ret_acquired, char ***ret_activatable); /* free the results */
functions.description: Lists currently owned names and activatable names on the bus, returning two string vectors. Caller must free the results.
requirements: bus must be connected.
ret_acquired and/or ret_activatable may be NULL or pointers to receive NULL-terminated arrays; caller must free them.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_get_name_creds
functions.signature: int sd_bus_get_name_creds(sd_bus *bus, const char *name, uint64_t mask, sd_bus_creds **ret); /* unref the result! */
functions.description: Retrieves credentials for a peer identified by a well-known name with fields specified by mask. Returns a new sd_bus_creds object that must be unrefed by the caller.
requirements: bus must be connected.
name must be a valid service name currently present.
mask selects which credential fields to fetch.
ret must be non-NULL; caller must unref the returned sd_bus_creds.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_get_name_machine_id
functions.description: Retrieves the 128-bit machine ID associated with the connection owning the given name.
requirements: bus must be connected.
name must be a valid service name.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_message_send
functions.description: Convenience: Sends the prepared message using its associated bus.
requirements: m must be a valid, sealed message bound to a bus.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_call_methodv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_call_methodv(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, sd_bus_message **ret_reply, const char *types, va_list ap);
functions.description: Convenience: Performs a synchronous method call with signature types and va_list arguments, returning a reply.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
types and ap must match the method input signature.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
ret_reply may be NULL or pointer to receive reply; caller must unref.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_call_method
functions.signature: int sd_bus_call_method(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, sd_bus_message **ret_reply, const char *types, ...);
functions.description: Convenience: Performs a synchronous method call with signature types and variadic arguments.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
types and variadic arguments must match the method input signature.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
ret_reply may be NULL or pointer to receive reply; caller must unref.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_call_method_asyncv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_call_method_asyncv(sd_bus *bus, sd_bus_slot **ret_slot, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_message_handler_t callback, void *userdata, const char *types, va_list ap);
functions.description: Convenience: Asynchronously issues a method call with signature types and va_list args; invokes callback on completion; returns a slot.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
types and ap must match the input signature.
callback may be NULL or provided.
ret_slot may be NULL or pointer to receive slot; unref when done.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_call_method_async
functions.signature: int sd_bus_call_method_async(sd_bus *bus, sd_bus_slot **ret_slot, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_message_handler_t callback, void *userdata, const char *types, ...);
functions.description: Convenience: Asynchronously issues a method call with variadic args; callback invoked on completion; returns a slot.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
types and variadic arguments must match the input signature.
callback may be NULL or provided.
ret_slot may be NULL or pointer to receive slot; unref when done.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_get_property
functions.signature: int sd_bus_get_property(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, sd_bus_message **ret_reply, const char *type);
functions.description: Convenience: Performs an org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get call to fetch a property of given type.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid (member is usually property name or "Get").
type is the expected type signature of the property value.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
ret_reply may be NULL or pointer to receive reply; caller must unref.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_get_property_trivial
functions.signature: int sd_bus_get_property_trivial(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, char type, void *ret);
functions.description: Convenience: Gets a simple (trivial) typed property directly into ret (by value) according to type.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
type must be a basic type code compatible with ret storage.
ret must be non-NULL.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_get_property_string
functions.signature: int sd_bus_get_property_string(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, char **ret); /* free the result! */
functions.description: Convenience: Gets a string property value and allocates a new string stored in ret. Caller must free.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL; caller must free the allocated string.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_get_property_strv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_get_property_strv(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, char ***ret); /* free the result! */
functions.description: Convenience: Gets a string array property and allocates a NULL-terminated array in ret. Caller must free.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL; caller must free the array.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_set_propertyv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_set_propertyv(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, const char *type, va_list ap);
functions.description: Convenience: Sets a property using org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Set with value described by type and va_list ap.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
type must match the value supplied in ap.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_set_property
functions.signature: int sd_bus_set_property(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_error *reterr_error, const char *type, ...);
functions.description: Convenience: Sets a property using a type signature and variadic value arguments.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
type and variadic args must match.
reterr_error may be NULL or pointer to receive error.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_returnv
functions.description: Sends a method return reply to an incoming call with values described by types and ap.
requirements: call must be a valid incoming method call message.
types and ap must match the expected reply signature.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_return
functions.description: Sends a method return reply to an incoming call with values described by types and variadic arguments.
requirements: call must be valid.
types and arguments must match reply signature.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_error
functions.description: Sends an error reply to an incoming method call using sd_bus_error e.
requirements: call must be valid.
e may be NULL or set; if provided, must be initialized per API.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_errorfv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_reply_method_errorfv(sd_bus_message *call, const char *name, const char *format, va_list ap) _sd_printf_(3, 0);
functions.description: Sends an error reply with specific error name and formatted message using va_list ap.
requirements: call must be valid.
name must be a valid D-Bus error name.
format/ap must form a valid printf-style message.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_errorf
functions.signature: int sd_bus_reply_method_errorf(sd_bus_message *call, const char *name, const char *format, ...) _sd_printf_(3, 4);
functions.description: Sends an error reply with specific error name and formatted message.
requirements: call must be valid.
name must be a valid error name.
format and variadic args must be valid.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_errno
functions.signature: int sd_bus_reply_method_errno(sd_bus_message *call, int error, const sd_bus_error *e);
functions.description: Sends an error reply derived from an errno code and optional sd_bus_error.
requirements: call must be valid.
error is an errno-style code.
e may be NULL or set.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_errnofv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_reply_method_errnofv(sd_bus_message *call, int error, const char *format, va_list ap) _sd_printf_(3, 0);
functions.description: Sends an errno-based error reply with a formatted message (va_list).
requirements: call must be valid.
error is errno-style.
format/ap must be valid.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_reply_method_errnof
functions.signature: int sd_bus_reply_method_errnof(sd_bus_message *call, int error, const char *format, ...) _sd_printf_(3, 4);
functions.description: Sends an errno-based error reply with a formatted message.
requirements: call must be valid.
error is errno-style.
format and variadic args must be valid.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_signalv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_signalv(sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, const char *types, va_list ap);
functions.description: Emits a signal from this connection at path/interface/member with arguments specified by types and va_list ap.
requirements: bus must be connected.
path/interface/member must be valid.
types/ap must match signal signature.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_signal
functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_signal(sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, const char *types, ...);
functions.description: Emits a signal with arguments described by types and variadic args.
requirements: bus must be connected.
path/interface/member must be valid.
types and arguments must match signature.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_signal_tov
functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_signal_tov(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, const char *types, va_list ap);
functions.description: Emits a signal targeted at a specific destination using va_list ap for arguments.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
types/ap must match signature.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_signal_to
functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_signal_to(sd_bus *bus, const char *destination, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, const char *types, ...);
functions.description: Emits a signal targeted at a specific destination using variadic arguments.
requirements: bus must be connected.
destination/path/interface/member must be valid.
types and variadic args must match.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_properties_changed_strv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_properties_changed_strv(sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, char **names);
functions.description: Emits a PropertiesChanged signal for the specified interface at path with a NULL-terminated list of property names.

path must be a valid object path.
interface must be a valid interface name.
names must be a NULL-terminated array of strings or NULL for none.

functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_properties_changed(sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *name, ...) _sd_sentinel_;
functions.description: Emits a PropertiesChanged signal specifying property names as a variadic list terminated by NULL (sentinel).
requirements: bus must be connected.

name list must be terminated by NULL due to _sd_sentinel_.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_object_added
functions.description: Emits an InterfacesAdded/ObjectManager notification that an object was added at path.

path must be a valid object path.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_object_removed
functions.description: Emits an InterfacesRemoved/ObjectManager notification that an object was removed at path.
requirements: bus must be connected.
path must be a valid object path.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.description: Emits InterfacesAdded for a list of interfaces (NULL-terminated array) at path.
requirements: bus must be connected.
path must be valid.
interfaces must be a NULL-terminated array of interface names.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_interfaces_added(sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, ...) _sd_sentinel_;
functions.description: Emits InterfacesAdded for one or more interfaces specified as a variadic list terminated by NULL.

path must be valid.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_interfaces_removed_strv
functions.description: Emits InterfacesRemoved for a list of interfaces (NULL-terminated array) at path.
requirements: bus must be connected.
path must be valid.
interfaces must be a NULL-terminated array.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_emit_interfaces_removed
functions.signature: int sd_bus_emit_interfaces_removed(sd_bus *bus, const char *path, const char *interface, ...) _sd_sentinel_;
functions.description: Emits InterfacesRemoved for one or more interfaces specified as a variadic NULL-terminated list.
requirements: bus must be connected.
path must be valid.
Argument list must be NULL-terminated due to sentinel.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_query_sender_creds
functions.description: Fetches credentials of the sender of message m according to mask, returning an sd_bus_creds object in ret.
requirements: m must be valid.
mask selects credential fields.
ret must be non-NULL; caller likely must unref (not explicitly stated here).
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_query_sender_privilege
functions.description: Checks whether the sender of message m has the specified Linux capability.
requirements: m must be valid.
capability must be a valid CAP_* value.
Returns >0 if allowed, 0 otherwise, or negative on error.

functions.name: sd_bus_match_signal
functions.signature: int sd_bus_match_signal(sd_bus *bus, sd_bus_slot **ret, const char *sender, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_message_handler_t callback, void *userdata);

functions.signature: int sd_bus_match_signal_async(sd_bus *bus, sd_bus_slot **ret, const char *sender, const char *path, const char *interface, const char *member, sd_bus_message_handler_t match_callback, sd_bus_message_handler_t install_callback, void *userdata);

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_new_from_pid
functions.signature: int sd_bus_creds_new_from_pid(sd_bus_creds **ret, pid_t pid, uint64_t creds_mask);
functions.description: Creates a new sd_bus_creds object by querying credentials of process pid according to creds_mask.

pid must identify an existing process the caller can query.
creds_mask selects which fields to fetch.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_new_from_pidfd
functions.signature: int sd_bus_creds_new_from_pidfd(sd_bus_creds **ret, int pidfd, uint64_t creds_mask);
functions.description: Creates a new sd_bus_creds object from a pidfd handle according to creds_mask.

creds_mask selects fields.

requirements: c may be NULL by convention; not explicitly stated.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_unref
functions.description: Decrements reference count of credentials object c and frees when zero. Returns NULL.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_mask
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of credential fields currently populated in c.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_augmented_mask
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of fields that could be obtained via augmentation if requested.
requirements: c must be valid.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_pid
functions.description: Fetches the process ID from the credentials object if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_pidfd_dup
functions.description: Returns a duplicated pidfd for the process, if available, through ret.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL; caller owns and must close the returned fd.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_ppid
functions.description: Gets the parent process ID from credentials, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_tid
functions.description: Gets the thread ID from credentials, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_uid
functions.description: Gets the real user ID from credentials, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_euid
functions.description: Gets the effective user ID from credentials, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_suid
functions.description: Gets the saved user ID, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_fsuid
functions.description: Gets the filesystem user ID, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_gid
functions.description: Gets the real group ID, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_egid
functions.description: Gets the effective group ID, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_sgid
functions.description: Gets the saved group ID, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_fsgid
functions.description: Gets the filesystem group ID, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.description: Gets a pointer to the supplementary group IDs array, if available.

ret must be non-NULL; returned pointer is owned by creds.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_tid_comm
functions.description: Gets the thread command name (comm), if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL; returned pointer is owned by creds.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_creds_get_exe
functions.description: Gets the executable path, if available.
requirements: c must be valid.
ret must be non-NULL; returned pointer is owned by creds.
Returns 0 or negative errno-style code.

functions.name: sd_bus_error_set

functions.name: sd_bus_error_setf
functions.signature: int sd_bus_error_setf(sd_bus_error *e, const char *name, const char *format, ...)  _sd_printf_(3, 4);
functions.description: Sets sd_bus_error e with error name and a printf-style formatted message.

format and variadic args must be valid.
Returns status code (errno-style negative on failure, 0 on success typically).

functions.name: sd_bus_error_setfv
functions.signature: int sd_bus_error_setfv(sd_bus_error *e, const char *name, const char *format, va_list ap) _sd_printf_(3,0);
functions.description: va_list variant of sd_bus_error_setf.
requirements: e must be non-NULL.

functions.name: sd_bus_error_set_errnofv

functions.name: sd_bus_error_copy
functions.description: Deep-copies sd_bus_error e into dest.

functions.name: sd_bus_error_move
functions.description: Moves the contents of e into dest, leaving e reset.

functions.name: sd_bus_error_is_set

functions.name: sd_bus_error_has_name

functions.name: sd_bus_error_add_map
functions.description: Registers an error name-to-code mapping table for automatic conversion between D-Bus errors and errno-style codes.

functions.name: sd_bus_path_encode_many

functions.name: sd_bus_path_decode

functions.name: sd_pid_get_session

requirements: pid must refer to a running process; system processes and 'shared' user processes are not attached to a session and cause an error
ret_session must be a non-NULL pointer to a char*
Caller owns returned memory and must free it with free()
Returns negative errno on error; >= 0 on success

Returns negative errno on error; >= 0 on success

functions.name: sd_path_lookup
functions.signature: int sd_path_lookup(uint64_t type, const char *suffix, char **ret);
functions.description: Resolves a single filesystem path for a well-known directory of the given type and returns it in a newly-allocated string. The type must identify one of the predefined SD_PATH_* entries in this header. If a suffix is provided, it is appended to the resolved base path (semantics of suffix are not documented here; typically it is a relative path component). Returns an integer status (systemd style: 0 or positive on success, negative errno-style code on failure). Use this for path types that resolve to a single directory; for search-path types consider sd_path_lookup_strv. The returned string is owned by the caller and must be freed.
requirements: type must be a valid SD_PATH_* value defined by this header (not _SD_PATH_INVALID).
ret must be non-NULL and point to a char* variable to receive an allocated NUL-terminated string.
On success, the caller takes ownership of *ret and must free the memory when done.
The return value must be checked; on failure an error code (negative errno-style) may be returned.

functions.name: sd_path_lookup_strv
functions.signature: int sd_path_lookup_strv(uint64_t type, const char *suffix, char ***ret);
functions.description: Resolves a search path for a well-known directory class and returns all candidate paths as a newly-allocated, NULL-terminated array of strings. The type must identify one of the predefined SD_PATH_* entries; this variant is intended for types that correspond to a search path (multiple directories). If a suffix is provided, it is appended to each resolved base path (exact suffix semantics are not documented here). Returns an integer status (systemd style: 0 or positive on success, negative errno-style code on failure). The returned array and its strings are owned by the caller and must be freed.
requirements: type must be a valid SD_PATH_* value defined by this header (not _SD_PATH_INVALID).
ret must be non-NULL and point to a char** variable to receive a newly-allocated NULL-terminated array of strings.
On success, the caller takes ownership of *ret and must free the array and all contained strings when done.
The return value must be checked; on failure an error code (negative errno-style) may be returned.

functions.name: sd_hwdb_ref
functions.description: Increase the reference count of an sd_hwdb object and return the same object. Use when sharing the handle across components to ensure proper lifetime management.
requirements: hwdb must be a valid, previously initialized sd_hwdb handle (e.g., returned from sd_hwdb_new or sd_hwdb_new_from_path).
The returned pointer is owned by the caller and must be released with sd_hwdb_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: sd_hwdb_unref
functions.description: Decrease the reference count of an sd_hwdb object and free it when the count drops to zero. Returns NULL for convenience so callers can write hwdb = sd_hwdb_unref(hwdb).
requirements: hwdb must be either NULL or a valid sd_hwdb handle obtained from this API.
After this call, the passed-in handle must not be used unless another reference remains elsewhere.
Callers must not free the object directly; use sd_hwdb_unref to release ownership.

functions.name: sd_hwdb_new
functions.description: Create and initialize a new hardware database (hwdb) object using the default search paths. On success, stores the new handle in *ret.
requirements: ret must be a non-NULL pointer to an sd_hwdb* variable to receive the created handle.
On success, the caller owns one reference to the returned handle and must release it with sd_hwdb_unref.
Return value is an integer status: 0 or positive on success, negative errno-style on failure (exact values not specified in this header).

functions.name: sd_hwdb_new_from_path
functions.description: Create and initialize a new hwdb object from a specific database file at the given path, instead of using default paths. On success, stores the handle in *ret.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string specifying the hwdb file to open.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to an sd_hwdb* variable to receive the created handle.
The path must refer to a valid hwdb database file readable by the process; otherwise a negative errno-style error is returned (exact codes not specified in this header).
On success, the caller owns one reference to the returned handle and must release it with sd_hwdb_unref.

functions.name: sd_hwdb_get
functions.signature: int sd_hwdb_get(sd_hwdb *hwdb, const char *modalias, const char *key, const char **value);
functions.description: Lookup a property value in the hwdb for a given modalias and key. On success, returns status and stores a pointer to the property's value string in *value. The returned string is const and must not be modified; lifetime and ownership are not documented here (likely tied to the hwdb object or the call).
requirements: hwdb must be a valid sd_hwdb handle.
modalias must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string indicating the match (e.g., a device modalias).
key must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string naming the property to look up.
value must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a const char* result; the pointed-to string must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Return value is an integer status; negative errno-style on failure or if not found (exact success code and not-found semantics are not specified in this header).

functions.name: sd_hwdb_seek
functions.description: Prepare enumeration of all properties associated with the given modalias. Typically followed by repeated calls to sd_hwdb_enumerate to iterate key/value pairs. Intended usage is reflected by the SD_HWDB_FOREACH_PROPERTY macro.
requirements: hwdb must be a valid sd_hwdb handle.
modalias must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Must be called before sd_hwdb_enumerate to initialize the enumeration state.
Return value is negative on error; non-negative on success (per usage in the provided macro).

functions.name: sd_hwdb_enumerate
functions.signature: int sd_hwdb_enumerate(sd_hwdb *hwdb, const char **key, const char **value);
functions.description: Iterate over properties prepared by the most recent sd_hwdb_seek call. On each successful step, stores pointers to the current key and value strings and returns >0. Returns 0 when enumeration is complete, and a negative value on error. The returned strings are const and must not be modified; lifetime/ownership are not documented here (likely valid until the next enumeration step or until the hwdb is modified/freed).
requirements: hwdb must be a valid sd_hwdb handle.
sd_hwdb_seek must have been successfully called on this hwdb before enumeration begins.
key and value must be non-NULL pointers to receive const char* results; the pointed-to strings must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Call sd_hwdb_enumerate repeatedly while the return value is >0; stop when it returns 0. Handle negative return values as errors.
